title: H01 Petavoxel AI Reconstruction of Human Cerebral Cortex Connectome
aiSystem: Flood-Filling Networks (Google Research) & Automated Synapse Classifiers
whyItMatters: First petavoxel-scale (1.4 PB) AI nanoscale 3D reconstruction of human cerebral cortex—mapping ~57,000 cells and 150 million synapses—uncovering previously unknown mirror-symmetric neurons and ultra-strong >50-synapse connections.
summary: Alexander Shapson-Coe, Jeff Lichtman (Harvard), Viren Jain (Google Research), and collaborators published in Science (May 2024) the highest-resolution 3D nanoscale connectome ever constructed of human brain tissue: a 1-cubic-millimeter surgical biopsy of human temporal cortex spanning all six cortical layers across 1.4 petabytes of multibeam electron microscopy. Google’s Flood-Filling Networks (FFNs) and neural synapse/cell-type classifiers reconstructed ~57,000 cells, 230 millimeters of blood vessels, and ~150 million synapses—revealing completely unexpected human neuroanatomy including mirror-symmetric deep-layer pyramidal neuron pairs, axonal whorls, and rare axon–dendrite pairs connected by more than 50 synapses.
technicalHighlights: AI Flood-Filling Networks segmented a 1.4-petabyte, 5,000-slice human cortical electron microscopy volume containing ~57,000 cells and ~150 million synapses.
Discovered previously unrecognized mirror-symmetric layer-6 triangular pyramidal neurons, giant multi-synaptic (>50-synapse) excitatory bridges, and mysterious axonal whorls.
Released publicly as the open H01 Neuroglancer atlas, demonstrating petascale AI pipelines required for future whole-mammalian-brain connectomics.
caveats: The tissue sample came from a single patient undergoing epilepsy surgery (though judged histologically healthy), and large-scale automated segmentation still required extensive human proofreading for error-free circuit tracing.

scoreRationale.foundational: First petavoxel AI reconstruction of human cerebral cortex, uncovering novel synaptic and cellular architectures.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly enabled the MICrONS mouse visual cortex connectome and roadmap toward whole-mouse-brain nanoscale mapping.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Science with an openly browsable 1.4 PB dataset and proofread ground-truth benchmarks.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed what would take centuries of manual human tracing across 1.4 petabytes into scalable automated neural segmentation.
